review_notes: I read the whole target file, the `PrimeMultiplicity` file it builds on, and all uses of `awayPrimeMultiplicityValuation_mk` (MvPolynomialAway.lean and the tests). I also checked Mathlib's `WithZero.exp_*` simp lemmas. I did not run Lean, so the claim that simp expands the right-hand side comes from reading `exp_sub`'s `@[simp]` attribute. I did not look for a loop. `isDomain_away` and the definition have no simp-interface problems. I considered a missing x = 0 companion lemma and did not report it, because nothing in the file or its uses needs one.

findings.problem: The lemma is tagged `@[simp]`, but its right-hand side `exp ((n : ℤ) - multiplicity p x)` is not in simp normal form. Mathlib has `@[simp] lemma exp_sub (a b : G) : exp (a - b) = exp a / exp b`. After this lemma fires, simp therefore rewrites the result again to `exp ↑n / exp ↑(multiplicity p x)`. That is not the form stated in the module docstring (`exp (n - multiplicity p x)`) or in the theorem. The simp set also contains `exp_add` and `inv_exp`, which push expressions toward other shapes. `PrimeMultiplicity.valuationDef_pow` avoids this by using `exp (-(n:ℤ))`, which has no simp rewrite. Every actual use of the lemma is an explicit `rw [...awayPrimeMultiplicityValuation_mk ...]` followed by `← exp_zero`, `exp_le_exp`, `exp_inj` or `congr 1; omega`. These rely on the unexpanded `exp (n - multiplicity)` shape, so the simp attribute is unused. It also makes `simp` output differ from the stated formula.
findings.proposed_change: Choose one orientation. Option A (smallest change): remove `@[simp]` and keep the lemma as an explicit `rw` rule. Option B: keep a simp lemma but state its right-hand side in the form simp reaches, `exp (n : ℤ) / exp (multiplicity p x : ℤ)`. Then keep the current statement as a separate non-simp lemma for the `rw` call sites, proved from it with `← exp_sub`. Either way, `simp` no longer turns an `Away.mk` valuation into a form that differs from the documented formula.
findings.benefit: `simp` and `rw` then agree on one canonical form for this valuation. Downstream proofs about `exp_le_exp`, `exp_inj` and `exp_zero` are not broken by a surprise division, and the simp attribute matches the lemma's documented and actual use.
